title: WPSB/185/2026 of VIVEK SHARMA Vs UNION OF INDIA

paras.text:
2026:UHC:2400-DB
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
THE HON'BLE CHIEF JUSTICE SHRI MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA
AND
THE HON'BLE JUSTICE SHRI SUBHASH UPADHYAY
6th April, 2026
Writ Petition (S/B) No. 185 of 2026
Vivek Sharma ------Petitioner
Versus
Union of India and & others -----Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Krishan Mohan Joshi, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned Deputy Solicitor General of India, assisted by
Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned Standing Counsel for the respondents.
JUDGMENT: (per Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)
1. The petitioner is presently holding the post of
Senior Commandant in CISF. He was promoted to the
said post and simultaneously transferred as Senior
Commandant at BHEL, Haridwar vide order dated
12.06.2024. On 24.03.2026, by the order impugned
herein he has been transferred from BHEL, Haridwar to
NTPC/CMP, Hazaribag. Aggrieved thereby, the instant
petition has been filed.
2. The contention of learned counsel for the
petitioner is that the tenure of the petitioner as per the
transfer policy (CISF Circular No. 14/2015) is three
years extendable by another one year due to
1

2026:UHC:2400-DB
administrative/operational exigencies. However, the
petitioner has been transferred without his completing
his tenure at BHEL, Haridwar.
3. The other submission is that the transfer is
not in public interest but has been passed to
accommodate one Deepak Kumar at BHEL, Haridwar, on
his own request.
4. Learned counsel for CISF has placed on
record the instructions received from the Director
General, CISF. It is stated that the transfer of Deepak
Kumar, Commandant to BHEL, Haridwar has been made
on compassionate ground considering his request. It is
stated that his spouse is employed with the
Uttarakhand Government and is posted at Narendra
Nagar, near Rishikesh, where she is undergoing
treatment for gynecological/obstetric complications
requiring continuous medical care. This situation has
significantly affected their family life. Previously he was
posted far away in Hazaribag, Jharkhand and even
during his tenure at FHQ, New Delhi, he could not
reside with his family.
5. In respect of the petitioner, it is admitted that
he has completed 1 year 9 months only at BHEL,
2

2026:UHC:2400-DB
Haridwar. However, the stand taken is that his children
are not at critical stage of education and CISF Unit,
NTPC/CMP, Hazaribag is a well established unit with
adequate schooling and medical facilities to support his
children's education and his mother's medical needs.
6. The further stand taken is that tenure
prescribed in the circular is only indicative and may be
extended or curtailed depending on administrative or
operational exigencies.
7. Paragraph 14 (ii) (iii) of the Circular are as
follows:-
"(ii) DG, CISF may transfer as officer whenever felt
necessary in public interest and on
administrative/operational exigencies / requirement.
(iii) Guidelines above do not confer any right,
whatsoever, upon any officer in matters of his
transfer/posting to any place."
8. The guidelines contained in the transfer policy
do not confer any right in favour of any employee to
claim posting and transfer at a particular location. The
circular is only in shape of guidelines but the overriding
factor is exigencies of service. Although, the petitioner
has been transferred to accommodate one Deepak
Kumar, but in the facts narrated above, it cannot be
3

2026:UHC:2400-DB
said that the transfer order is vitiated by any
extraneous consideration. Consequently, we decline to
interfere with the said order.
9. However, we leave it open to the petitioner to
represent to the concerned authority, in case, there is
any hardship being faced by the petitioner on account
of his transfer. In the event, any such representation is
made, it shall be decided within three weeks from the
date it is made.
10. The writ petition stands disposed of.
11. Pending application, if any, also stands
disposed of.

(MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C.J.)
 (SUBHASH UPADHYAY, J.)
Dated: 06.04.2026
Kaushal
